On 2025-08-03 09:12, Luca Martinez wrote:
> We're starting the formal handoff for our on-prem Redwood deployment and need alignment on the CSR template/fields you will accept (we want to playback a CSR and have it match what your runtime expects)...

Hi Luca — below are the minimum CSR constraints and recommended metadata for CSR playback. I attached a trimmed example CSR template that maps to the list.

Minimum CSR / certificate guidance (short):
- Subject: CN is optional if SANs present; Redwood prefers SAN-first. Please include primary service FQDN as a SAN.
- SANs: include service FQDN (svc.<tenant>.<domain>), any internal alias used by LB, and at least one IP if callers use IP-based checks (we prefer hostnames).
- Key type: ECDSA P-256 or RSA 2048 (P-256 recommended for new deploys).
- Extensions: basicConstraints CA:FALSE; keyUsage: digitalSignature,keyEncipherment; extendedKeyUsage: serverAuth,clientAuth (if mTLS expected).
- CSR metadata: include a clear ORG/O field with tenant ID for traceability.
- Lifetime & rotation: requested validity <= 397 days and rotation window >= 7 days before expiry for automated rotation.

CSR playback process (what you'll get back):
- Parsed field report (subject/SANs/alg/extensions).
- Warnings for missing recommended SANs or unexpected wildcard usage.
- A recommended cert profile (e.g., enable OCSP stapling & stapling interval).

Split-horizon / DNS considerations (quick):
- If you use a private hosted zone in Route53, we recommend we accept an explicit delegation (ns records) from the customer side. Redwood can also consume a fixed CNAME pointing to the private endpoint, but delegation is more resilient for failover automation.
- TTL recommendation: 30s–60s for failover-sensitive records, 300s for internal-only SRV records where clients cache aggressively.
- For SRV-based discovery, ensure TTLs are low and include health-check-driven weight updates so we can coordinate automated failovers.

Attachment: acme_csr_template.pem.stub (sample adapted to our parser)

Let me know if we should include mTLS client cert fields in the playback. If ACME wants mutual TLS for internal control-plane calls, include clientAuth EKU in the CSR.

Adding ops detail from the runtime side — options and tradeoffs for TLS termination and resolver choreography:

Option A — Customer-terminates TLS at on-prem LB (preferred for data isolation):
- Customer holds private key, Redwood connects over private peering/VPN to internal endpoint.
- Requires a Route53 private hosted zone with delegation to customer NS or static CNAMEs to the LB.
- Pros: keys never leave customer; simpler audit.
- Cons: less ability for Redwood to apply automatic fallback routing during capacity issues.

Option B — Redwood-terminates TLS at private Redwood endpoint (managed cert):
- Redwood can alternate endpoints (region/pooled capacity) and update DNS during failover.
- Requires explicit DNS delegation or a stable CNAME target and agreed SNI mapping.
- Pros: smoother failover automation, faster rollbacks.
- Cons: customer must trust Redwood-managed certs / key escrow model.

Operational asks for either path:
- Provide a private-zone change window and a tacit maintainer contact (email + PagerDuty).
- For failover, prefer low TTLs (30s) on the primary A/CNAME and keep SRV TTLs at 60–120s.
- We recommend OCSP stapling enabled and a monitored stapling latency SLO.

I've attached a simple network sketch showing where Redwood's private gateway sits relative to your VPC and the resolver expectations. This illustrates both Option A and B.
